snapshots.name: Heraclitus
snapshots.body: The Greek philosopher of flux, cited for likening the world to a child’s game and for having withdrawn to the temple of Artemis at Ephesus.

snapshots.name: Adam
snapshots.body: The biblical first man, named as the ancestor on whom the curse of humanity's unpayable debt to God is fixed ('original sin').

snapshots.name: Richard Wagner

snapshots.name: Ludwig Feuerbach

snapshots.name: Stendhal

snapshots.name: Pygmalion

snapshots.name: G. W. F. Hegel

snapshots.name: Socrates
snapshots.body: The Athenian philosopher, cited as the one exception among philosophers who married, said to have done so, ironically, only to prove the rule.

snapshots.name: Buddha

snapshots.name: King Vicvamitra

snapshots.name: Shankara

snapshots.name: Teresa of Ávila

snapshots.name: Leo Tolstoy

snapshots.name: Ernest Renan
snapshots.body: The French historian of religion Nietzsche mocks, via the phrase 'Renan parfum,' as a scented, half-priest, half-satyr type among modern historians.

snapshots.name: Anacreon

snapshots.name: Charles the Bold
snapshots.body: Duke of Burgundy, whose defiant words against Louis XI ('I fight the universal spider') Nietzsche borrows for humanity's stance toward God.

snapshots.name: Louis XI
